name: סכום טור טלסקופי – a/n−a/(n+s) בעזרת שברים חלקיים (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Given the series

\[ \sum_{n\geq {{CT:0}}} {{CT:1}} \]

Expand the general term into partial fractions in order to find the sum of the infinite series.

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Split the term into two fractions; in the partial sum almost everything cancels, and only the first \({{CT:2}}\) positive fractions are left in the limit.
Step 1 — Partial fractions
Since \(\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n+{{CT:2}}}=\frac{ {{CT:2}} }{n(n+{{CT:2}})}\),

\[ {{CT:1}}={{CT:3}}\left(\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n+{{CT:2}}}\right) \]

Step 2 — The partial sum
Add the terms from \(n={{CT:0}}\) to \(n=N\). Every fraction \(\frac{1}{m}\) with \({{CT:4}}\le m\le N\) appears once with a plus sign and once with a minus sign, so it cancels:

\[ S_N={{CT:3}}\left(\sum_{n={{CT:0}}}^{ {{CT:5}} }\frac{1}{n}-\sum_{n=N+1}^{N+{{CT:2}}}\frac{1}{n}\right) \]

Step 3 — The limit
Each of the \({{CT:2}}\) fractions \(\frac{1}{N+1},\dots,\frac{1}{N+{{CT:2}}}\) tends to 0 as \(N\to\infty\), so

\[ \sum_{n\geq {{CT:0}}} {{CT:1}}={{CT:3}}\sum_{n={{CT:0}}}^{ {{CT:5}} }\frac{1}{n}={{CT:3}}\cdot {{CT:6}}={{CT:7}} \]

on_true.feedback: Well done your answer is correct.
This is the wrong answer. Note that the sum here does not start from 1 but rather from {{CT:8}}, perhaps this was your mistake.

on_false.feedback: Sorry you got the wrong answer. Note that in this exercise the ``telescopic series'' is not as simple as the one given in the example because the cancellation is happenning between summands that are farther away from each other in the series. Writing the general term as \(\frac{ {{CT:3}} }{n}-\frac{ {{CT:3}} }{n+{{CT:2}}}\), each term \(\frac{ {{CT:3}} }{n}\) cancels with the term \(-\frac{ {{CT:3}} }{n}\) that appears {{CT:9}} places earlier. So in the partial sums only the first {{CT:9}} positive terms survive, those with \(n={{CT:0}},\ldots,{{CT:5}}\), while the last {{CT:9}} negative terms tend to \(0\).
